Business Continuity Planning

A structured engagement that identifies your critical business processes, sets recovery priorities, and produces a continuity plan your management team has rehearsed.

Discuss This Service ↗What’s included ↓
Typical duration
4–6 weeks
Format
Fixed-scope project, reviewed yearly
Works with
Management, IT, operations, and finance
Result
A tested business continuity plan

WHO IT IS FOR

Built for teams
like yours.

  • Medium enterprises with no written continuity plan, or one that has never been tested
  • Companies asked by banks, insurers, regulators, or major customers for a continuity plan
  • Organizations with multiple sites that depend on shared systems

WHAT’S INCLUDED

What the engagement covers

The exact scope is confirmed in writing before work begins, based on your systems, priorities, and existing work.

01

Business impact analysis

Identify critical processes, the systems and people they depend on, and how the impact of downtime grows over time.

02

Recovery priorities

Agree the order of recovery and the acceptable downtime for each critical process.

03

Continuity strategies

Practical ways to keep working, such as alternate sites, manual workarounds, and system recovery.

04

Roles and communication

Who declares an incident, who decides, and how staff, customers, and partners are informed.

05

Plan documentation

A clear, usable continuity plan with contact lists, checklists, and decision points.

06

Tabletop exercise

A facilitated scenario exercise with management to test the plan and improve it.

WHAT YOU RECEIVE

Deliverables your
team can use.

  • Business impact analysis
  • Recovery priorities and objectives
  • Business continuity plan
  • Crisis communication guide
  • Tabletop exercise report with improvements
01

Decisions made in advance

Priorities and authority are agreed before a crisis, not during one.

02

03

Confidence for stakeholders

Banks, insurers, and customers see a tested plan, not a template.

QUESTIONS

Common questions
about this service.

Something else on your mind? Ask our team ↗

How is this different from disaster recovery?

Disaster recovery restores IT systems. Business continuity covers the whole business: people, sites, suppliers, communication, and the order in which operations resume.

How often should the plan be updated?

At least once a year, and after major changes such as a new site, system, or organizational structure.

Do you write it for us or with us?

With you. A plan only works if your managers know it, so we run short working sessions and a tabletop exercise with your team.
